stem: In the figure shown, \(ABCD\) is a rectangle with \(AB = 10\) and \(BC = 6\), and point \(P\) lies on \(\overline{DC}\). What is the area of triangle \(ABP\)?
solution: Since \(\overline{DC}\) is parallel to \(\overline{AB}\) and the rectangle is \(6\) tall, the height from \(P\) to \(\overline{AB}\) is \(6\) no matter where \(P\) is on \(\overline{DC}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(10 \cdot 6\), the area of the whole rectangle; the triangle is half of it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}(10)(6)\); the \(\frac{1}{2}\) was applied twice.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(2(10 + 6)\), the perimeter of the rectangle, not an area.

verify:
P=figure['points']
assert P['B'][0]==10 and P['C'][1]==6 and P['P'][1]==6 and 0<=P['P'][0]<=10
o=['A','B','P']
ans=Rational(1,2)*abs(sum(P[o[i]][0]*P[o[(i+1)%3]][1]-P[o[(i+1)%3]][0]*P[o[i]][1] for i in range(3)))
assert ans==30
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
